editorial.marketOverview: U.S. equities are closed for the weekend. Reuters' Friday closing report showed Nasdaq -5.28% and the semiconductor index down about 11%; the prior secondary QQQ closing observation was -5.67%, Nvidia -14.01%. AP independently described the steep technology-led selling. These are Friday returns, not Saturday prices. The bearish baseline remains elevated downside risk for November 23–25.
editorial.whatChanged: The 22:38 EST weekend reassessment found no fresh U.S. cash-market session and no new Open Watch catalyst: the curated file contains 174 entries, last updated 00:44:37 UTC November 21. Fresh review of the November 20 Reuters/AP close and November 23–27 calendar did not identify an incremental event that changes the expected three-session path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor leadership is deeply negative and reported breadth was weak, consistent with defensive positioning. Reuters' Friday VIX around 37 and 10Y around 4.93% are rounded historical observations; the previous 2Y 4.65% is not synchronized with the 10Y, while the older 4.94% and 4.65% yield pair implies +29 basis points. Current VXN, FedWatch and maturity-matched oil remain unverified. Potential AI policy or valuation catalysts should not be presented as proven individual causes of Friday's decline.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 is a test of whether forced selling persists or oversold covering develops. Tuesday November 24 semiconductor and AI infrastructure earnings may test leadership; Wednesday November 25 PCE/GDP and other macro releases plus Beige Book increase event risk. A sustained bounce requires breadth and volatility confirmation; absent that, bearish continuation remains the base case.
editorial.bullCase: Deeply oversold conditions and Treasury safe-haven demand can facilitate a relief rally, but the evidence threshold is coordinated QQQ and SOX/SMH improvement, better breadth and retreating VXN/VIX on Monday and Tuesday. None is confirmed in the weekend interval.
editorial.bearCase: The Friday closing selloff, roughly 11% semiconductor index loss and high volatility signal a fragile tape. Continued AI hardware weakness, disappointing earnings or unfavorable macro repricing could produce further downside; none of those future outcomes is yet observed.
editorial.watchNext: Check Monday synchronized QQQ/SOX/SMH, VXN/VIX and advance-decline breadth, current 10Y/2Y and direct CME FedWatch, contract-matched Brent/WTI; verify earnings for HPE/Zoom Monday and ADI/Dell/HP Tuesday, plus Wednesday 08:30 ET PCE/GDP and 14:00 ET Beige Book. Monitor Open Watch for genuinely new events.
